blocks.content: A readiness probe checks whether a container is ready to receive traffic, unlike a liveness probe, a failure here does not restart anything, it simply, temporarily, pulls the Pod out of a Service's traffic rotation.
1. Is This Container Ready for Traffic?
blocks.text: 1. Is This Container Ready for Traffic?

blocks.content: A readiness probe asks a genuinely different question from liveness, not "is this container broken and needs restarting," but "should this container be receiving real user traffic right now."

blocks.alt: A different question entirely, about traffic readiness, not container health

blocks.content: This connects directly to the Endpoint topic in the Services module, a failing readiness probe removes that Pod from the Service's Endpoints list, kube-proxy simply stops routing traffic to it, without touching the Pod itself at all.

blocks.alt: A direct connection to the Endpoints mechanism covered in the Services module

blocks.content: 3. The Key Difference From Liveness: No Restart
blocks.text: 3. The Key Difference From Liveness: No Restart

blocks.content: This is the single most important distinction between the two probe types, a readiness failure never restarts the container, it just temporarily takes it out of rotation, the container keeps running exactly as it was.

blocks.alt: No restart, ever, purely a traffic routing decision

blocks.content: This is exactly the right tool for a Pod that is legitimately still starting up, or briefly overloaded and needs a moment to catch up, situations where restarting would be actively counterproductive, but sending it traffic right now would also be a mistake.

blocks.alt: Situations where restarting would make things worse, not better

blocks.content: An application that needs a few seconds to warm up a cache or establish a database connection pool before it can genuinely serve requests correctly should use a readiness probe to hold off traffic until that warm-up genuinely finishes.

blocks.alt: Traffic held off deliberately, until the app is genuinely ready to handle it well

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A readiness probe decides whether a Pod should receive traffic right now, a failure removes it from Service Endpoints, it never restarts the container.
This is the right tool for temporary, recoverable states, a slow startup or brief overload, where restarting would only make the situation worse.
